data.goal: Test pyprovides find against E086 import error corpus to measure resolution success rate

data.summary: Evaluated pyprovides resolver against known aliases from discrimination test: 16/19 resolved via alias/exact, 3 failed (pkg_resources via setuptools .pth mechanism, ldap via python-ldap no-wheel, pysftp not in top 500)

Ran pyprovides find against 19 discrimination test probes: 15/19 resolved (78.9%), 4 failed (attr name collision, pysftp not in top 500, pkg_resources via .pth, ldap no-wheel). The resolver is functional for the core use case.

Built and tested fix-import integration: pyprovides fix-import command runs a command, detects ModuleNotFoundError/ImportError from stderr, extracts module names, and suggests correct PyPI distributions to install. All 27 tests pass including 6 new fix_import tests.

data.next: Measure actual usage: integrate fix-import into a developer workflow (e.g., as a shell wrapper or pre-commit hook) and measure time-to-fix for import errors vs manual 'pip install <module>' baseline
data.summary: Built and tested fix-import integration for pyprovides resolver. The pyprovides fix-import command runs a user command, captures stderr, detects ModuleNotFoundError/ImportError patterns, extracts module names, and uses the pyprovides find resolver to suggest correct PyPI distributions to install. Evaluated against 19 discrimination test probes: 15/19 (78.9%) resolved via alias/exact/stdlib methods. Failures: attr (name collision with 'attr' package), pysftp (not in top 500), pkg_resources (setuptools .pth mechanism), ldap (python-ldap no wheel). All 27 tests pass (17 existing + 6 new fix_import tests + 4 find_provider tests).
